rule_en: used to + base = a past habit or STATE that is no longer true. would + base = a repeated past action (a routine) — but NOT for states (be, have, know, like).
rule_bn: অতীতের অভ্যাস বা অবস্থা (যা এখন নেই) → used to; অতীতে বারবার করা কাজ → would; কিন্তু অবস্থা বোঝাতে would নয়, used to।

sessions.title: Spot the Error
sessions.instruction_en: Tap the wrong word, then choose the fix.

items.prompt_en: When I was new, I use to ask the seniors for help every day
items.explain_en: The correct past-habit form is 'used to' with a 'd', not the bare 'use to'.

items.prompt_en: Before the migration, our org would be much slower than it is now
items.explain_en: 'would' cannot describe a past state with 'be', so a past condition that ended needs 'used to be'.

items.prompt_en: I used to working late before I learned how to delegate tasks
items.explain_en: 'used to' takes the base verb, so it is 'used to work', never 'used to working'.

items.prompt_en: Did you used to deploy on Fridays at your old company
items.explain_en: After the auxiliary 'did', the base form 'use to' is required, not 'used to'.

items.prompt_en: I would have an old laptop that crashed during every long build
items.explain_en: 'have' here is a past state of possession, so it needs 'used to have', not 'would'.

items.prompt_en: She would know every Apex governor limit by heart back then
items.explain_en: 'know' is a state verb, so a past state that ended takes 'used to know', not 'would'.

items.prompt_en: Every Friday afternoon we would deploying the new release to production
items.explain_en: 'would' for a repeated past routine takes the base verb, giving 'would deploy'.

items.prompt_en: I would like working alone, but now I really enjoy pairing with teammates
items.explain_en: 'like' is a state verb, so a past preference that changed needs 'used to like', not 'would'.

items.prompt_en: I didn't used to write unit tests until my mentor finally insisted on it
items.explain_en: After the negative auxiliary 'didn't', the base form 'use to' is correct, not 'used to'.

items.prompt_en: When the team was tiny, our codebase would be easy to understand
items.explain_en: A past state with 'be' that is no longer true takes 'used to be', since 'would' cannot mark states.

sessions.title: Choose & Fill
sessions.instruction_en: Tap the correct option or chip.

items.prompt_en: Before we adopted Salesforce, our team ___ track every lead in a spreadsheet.
items.explain_en: For a past habit that is no longer true, use 'used to' (with -d), not 'use to'.

items.prompt_en: ___ you use to write Apex triggers before switching to Flows?
items.explain_en: In questions the past is carried by 'did', so the main verb drops the -d: 'Did you use to...?'

items.prompt_en: Every Friday after the sprint, the team ___ get coffee together and review the demo.
items.explain_en: A repeated past routine (an action) can take 'would' + base verb, just like 'used to'.

items.prompt_en: I ___ a junior developer, but now I lead the integrations team.
items.explain_en: 'Be' is a state, so only 'used to' works here, not 'would'.

items.prompt_en: She ___ know much about Salesforce, but after the course she became an admin.
items.explain_en: 'Know' is a state verb, so only 'used to' is correct; 'would' cannot describe a state.

items.prompt_en: We ___ deploy manually every night before we set up the CI pipeline.
items.explain_en: A past habit no longer true takes 'used to' + base verb.

items.prompt_en: Did your manager ___ review every pull request himself?
items.explain_en: After 'did', the verb loses the -d, so it is 'use to'.

items.prompt_en: On long deploys, my old teammate ___ order pizza for everyone in the office.
items.explain_en: A repeated past action (routine) takes 'would' + base verb.

items.prompt_en: He used to ___ a long commute, but now he works from home.
items.explain_en: 'Used to' is followed by the base verb, so 'have', not 'having' or 'had'.

items.prompt_en: She ___ every Salesforce shortcut, but now she relies on the AI assistant.
items.explain_en: 'Know' is a state verb, so use 'used to know', not 'would'.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.

items.explain_en: Negative form is 'didn't use to', not 'didn't used to'.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: Every morning she would check the deployment logs .
items.explain_en: 'would' + base verb fits a repeated past routine ('every morning').

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: We used to have a smaller team .
items.explain_en: 'have' is a state, so use 'used to have', not 'would have'.
